reviews.text: The pacing is hopelessly unwieldly, with unnecessary deviations from the original film, added characters who don’t really have purpose and do not propel the plot, and new songs that are not up to Disney standards.
reviews.author: Lee Zumpe

reviews.text: Robert Zemeckis’ live-action film has gorgeous, seamless animation and revels in its seductive timelessness.
reviews.author: Mini Anthikad-Chhibber

reviews.text: Pinocchio boasts a more thematically impactful ending than the original but fails to deliver a new version of the famous childhood tale with the same magic and allure of the past.
reviews.author: Manuel São Bento

reviews.text: The movie doesn’t spark much magic like the original film does & just is very basic..
reviews.author: Zach Pope

reviews.text: For a film about a wooden boy who wants to become real and learn about what it means to be a person, Pinocchio (2022) is lifeless. Even Hanks, who has spent a good portion of his career playing charming, loveable characters, is bland in this adaptation.
reviews.author: Tina Kakadelis

reviews.text: Go build your own wooden doll. Even that will be more productive than watching this Robert Zemeckis directorial.
reviews.author: Pramit Chatterjee

reviews.text: The faithfulness of this film sees it play justified homage to its inspiration, although often at the expense of offering anything particularly worthy of the whole remake.
reviews.author: Tori Brazier

reviews.text: A sparkling reimagining of the indelible 1940 Disney classic that manages to pay homage to the original — and to the 1883 Carlos Collodi story that inspired it — while also weaving new layers of magic into the proceedings.
reviews.author: Mike Scott

reviews.text: Pinocchio will surely be a hit with families and will primarily be enjoyed by parents and children...However, audiences outside the target demographic will likely find this to be very surface-level and predictably average.
reviews.author: Aaron Phillips

reviews.text: They allow for some good emotional moments with a story that we've known before. Tom Hands does a good job as Geppetto & leads to the human connection to this story. Some times it feels like to much of a direct copy & doesn't boast for much rewatchability
reviews.author: Samuel Leggett Jr.

reviews.text: It might not be “Lion King” levels of bad, but it’s certainly “Mulan” levels of hollow and forgettable.
reviews.author: Felix Vasquez Jr.

reviews.text: All in all, Pinocchio ends up as a frustrating experience. It never feels like the characters had arcs, even if that’s what the film wants you to believe.
reviews.author: Jonathan Sim

reviews.text: ...manages enough charm, inventiveness, and technical innovation to be worth the effort.
reviews.author: Josh Larsen

reviews.text: unlikely to be remembered as the definitive version – just think of how quickly most other Disney remakes have disappeared from public consciousness. However, it is a sincere and polished attempt to walk in the footsteps of a masterpiece.
reviews.author: Victoria Luxford

reviews.text: For a story about a wooden puppet wanting to become a real boy, Zemeckis’ woeful approach with not-so-deep-fake animation visually destroys the narrative.
reviews.author: Liam Maguren

reviews.text:
"I'm a real boy!"
... and a piece of **** movie.
reviews.author: Adam Olinger

reviews.text: Pinocchio is bad, but it’s not inventively bad like Cats. It’s boringly bad, neither bold nor unique enough to be bad in a fun way.
reviews.author: Sarah Marrs

reviews.text: This dull recreation of the animated film doesn’t strive for anything more than what was contained in the original version of this film and actually delivers less.
reviews.author: John Kirk

reviews.text: Disney’s remake of its 1940 animated classic Pinocchio is just as bad as you’ve heard.
reviews.author: Eileen Jones

reviews.text: From the classic “When You Wish Upon a Star” to the character designs, Robert Zemeckis never imbues this film with anything authentic or original.
reviews.author: Alex Maidy

reviews.text: Although this live-action version of Pinocchio mostly stays with the story, it is not as seamless and entertaining as Disney’s 1940 animated classic.
reviews.author: Betty Jo Tucker

reviews.text: If you have youngsters, they'll probably enjoy this live-action/animation reboot. According to John Hooper & Anna Kraczna, who wrote a recent Penguin Classics treatment, 'Seldom has a work of literature been so overshadowed by its celluloid adaptations.'
reviews.author: Susan Granger

reviews.text: It was saddening to watch a great director not have his heart in this particular live-action/animated hybrid. Any heart or soul would have sufficed even if he already gave us his best version of the Pinocchio story with Forrest Gump.
reviews.author: Erik Childress

reviews.text: Sweet and endearing, the live-action Pinocchio is a great watch for the kids of today, while adults might find themselves longing for the original.
reviews.author: Gabi Zietsman

reviews.text: The bar was set low, and they couldn't even meet that.
reviews.author: EJ Moreno

reviews.text: Pinocchio is a frustratingly dry, functional and uninventive rendition of a fairytale that has somehow resisted cultural updates despite its morally elastic nature.
reviews.author: Rahul Desai

reviews.text: There's no real need to keep turning movies that have thrived in animation into awkward live-action updates, just as Pinocchio didn't have to turn into a real boy to become worthier.
reviews.author: Francisca Tinoco

reviews.text: I didn't hate it, I didn't love it, I liked parts of it, but I'm deeply disappointed by the overall effort.
reviews.author: Wade Major

reviews.text: A lovely and welcome antidote to the heat.
reviews.author: Lael Loewenstein

reviews.text: If you’re going to tackle this material, start from scratch or don’t start at all. As it stands, this version of Pinocchio is almost as pointless as Tim Burton’s Dumbo. I hate pulling out the D-word, but if the wooden shoe fits….
reviews.author: Steven Prokopy

reviews.text: faithful to the original and with an ad hoc final for modern times, this new version of Pinocchio simply can't seem to jellify. [Full Review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Laura Hiros

reviews.text: Just as Pinocchio wasn’t a real boy to start, this wasn’t a real movie – and there’s almost no chance it learnt enough lessons to become one with a soul.
reviews.author: Wenlei Ma

reviews.text: Frequent peril in live-action/CGI version of classic tale.
reviews.author: Jennifer Green

reviews.text: Not even Tom Hanks in front of the camera or Robert Zemeckis behind it  can make this blatantly opportunistic effort resonate.
reviews.author: Robert W. Butler

reviews.text: Even by Disney live-action remake standards, [Pinocchio] is quite subpar and it’s all because it tries way too hard at everything to the point that it no longer becomes enjoyable.
reviews.author: Mat Brunet

reviews.text: The movie falls in two camps. One adds new stuff that feels like it serves no other purpose than to pad the runtime... or two, does exactly what the animation did, it just doesn't do it nearly as well.
reviews.author: Jeremy Jahns

reviews.text: Hi-Diddle-Dee-Dee, it didn’t work for me.
reviews.author: Peter Travers

reviews.text: Here, they have unfortunately decided to intrude on the 19th century European setting and freshen it up with Honest John talking about social media influencers and acting like he’s snapping a photo with a cell phone. Huh?
reviews.author: Lynn Venhaus

reviews.text: Dull and uninspired.
reviews.author: Kristen Maldonado

reviews.text: Like the previous Disney remakes, it’s faithful and watchable but an unnecessary retread of a superior film that should have been left alone.
reviews.author: Loren King

reviews.text: The film possesses an obvious “wow” factor visually. Zemeckis’ films usually do in some form. What it can’t make up for, however, is the feeling that had he kept this story and running time closer to the original it would have kept its sense of whimsy.
reviews.author: George M. Thomas

reviews.text: Somehow the film feels inert compared with the 1940 animated classic, like it’s assembled by an AI program and just going through the motions.
reviews.author: Tom Meek

reviews.text: Pinocchio feels manufactured to appease everyone, with nary an original bone in its wooden body.
reviews.author: Alex Saveliev

reviews.text: It would be hard to remake an animated classic and match the same level of adoration. While new additions are made that elevate its story, Pinocchio is just another Disney remake that never really proves why it should exist.
reviews.author: Sara Clements

reviews.text: A beloved tale, then – but in Zemeckis’s hands, a cold, flat, witless and astoundingly odd affair... the entire fiasco looks and sounds like a cheap and charmless pantomime.
reviews.author: Chris Wasser

reviews.text: A misguided redo.
reviews.author: Randy Myers

reviews.text: Agreeable enough but completely forgettable film that's uninterested in charting new ground...
reviews.author: Brandon Zachary

reviews.text: The strings are off, with Tom Hanks still being a delight and much for the kids to enjoy. And still, this Pinocchio is mediocre at best.
reviews.author: Leo Brady

reviews.text: While Pinocchio has some new ideas and songs, it’s plagued by the same issues of every other live-action remake. Hopefully Guillermo del Toro’s forthcoming Pinocchio will be the reimagining audiences were hoping for.
reviews.author: Andrew Murray

reviews.text: Pinocchio ends up as another unnecessary remake that’s mostly forgettable.
reviews.author: Neil Soans

reviews.text: Results in an extremely comfortable film, superficial, flimsy, inoffensive, unreflective, and above all, unremarkable... [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Erick Estrada

reviews.text: Instead of capturing the old-school charm of the original, the new film looks as dead-eyed as one of Zemeckis’s motion-capture characters, as it recites the familiar fable of the puppet who wanted to be a boy.
reviews.author: David Sims

reviews.text: A dispiriting retelling of what should be an enchanting tale. It realizes and magnifies all of Hollywood’s worst tendencies when it comes to modern blockbuster filmmaking.
reviews.author: Cody Dericks

reviews.text: A hybrid with a blend of actors, animation, and CGI that doesn't know who its audience is, losing everyone in the process. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Pablo O. Scholz

reviews.text: Pinocchio... shows that it may be time to stop replicating what already exists.  [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: José Roberto Landaverde

reviews.text: Pinocchio is about as boring and disastrous as Disney live-action remakes get with its uninspired writing and directing, terrible performances, and horrid animation.
reviews.author: Joey Rambles

reviews.text: There's an overabundance of unnecessary concessions to modern taste in this effects-driven, CGI-animated remake, but it moves along pretty nicely—and they haven't broken it.
reviews.author: Peter Canavese

reviews.text: There’s a reason Disney’s original film is something people still treasure 82 years after it came out, and there’s a reason this new Pinocchio will hardly be remembered one year from now.
reviews.author: Fletcher Powell

reviews.text: Going down the whole list of all the ways in which this film is a tedious, stilted re-enactment of the original would get incredibly depressing quickly.
reviews.author: Tim Brayton

reviews.text: Though a well-crafted fantasy film for kids, it's emotionally a cold one.
reviews.author: Dennis Schwartz

reviews.text: I honestly loved Pinocchio from beginning to end.
reviews.author: Richard Propes

reviews.text: The story of the boy who wants to be real becomes a contradictory, even cautionary tale about how bringing life to the lifeless can go terribly wrong.
reviews.author: Simon Foster

reviews.text: Sadly, the changes made to the original are wooden headed, adding nearly a half-hour to the movie’s running time and sapping the story of much of its charm.
reviews.author: Russ Simmons

reviews.text: Flaws aside, though, it’s a much more respectable remake than many in the clunkily branded “Disney Live-Action Reimaginings” line.
reviews.author: Sean Collier

reviews.text: “Pinocchio” is no different from a good band covering a standard without bringing much originality to the arrangement.
reviews.author: Alci Rengifo

reviews.text: With tangled strings and meandering storytelling, Pinocchio is a musical misfire that seemingly sets out to annihilate everything that made its animated counterpart so enjoyable.
reviews.author: Chris Sawin

reviews.text: …perhaps little kids don’t mind almost every element being a downgrade on the 1940’s film, but adults certainly will…
reviews.author: Eddie Harrison

reviews.text: Disney is so obsessed with recreating iconic scenes and characters that they neglect the emotional side of the story.
reviews.author: Korey Coleman

reviews.text: Re-Watch The Original Instead Of This Wooden Remake.
reviews.author: Vanessa Armstrong

reviews.text: It's not an awful film but bringing the animated characters into the real world doesn't add anything to the story. Rather, it points up what is most charming about animation's ability to suspend belief.
reviews.author: Andrea Chase

reviews.text: Independent of the emotional resonance that Hank brings to this film, Zemeckis' Pinocchio is up there with A Christmas Carol and Beowulf, movies with spectacular cinematography built around simple and imperfect narratives. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Juanma Fernández París

reviews.text: Strange in all the backlash because it pretty much followed the 1940 film., however Tom Hanks really needs to retire all accents after this summer. There is a freshness to how alive the puppet is, and those who have nightmares about puppets will relate.
reviews.author: Patrick McDonald

reviews.text: Chances are it’ll be remembered about as well as the live-action Dumbo movie. Yeah, I forgot that existed too.
reviews.author: Andrea Thompson

reviews.text: A faithful adaptation to the Disney classic that doesn’t pull its punches on the weird and disturbing elements.
reviews.author: Kevin Carr

reviews.text: A mixed bag of boyish fear and yearning, sentiment, frightening action, tedious exposition and middling music.
reviews.author: James Verniere

reviews.text: Zemeckis doesn't take the time to dig into the depth that the story could offer and instead, chooses a CGI adventure... [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Emiliano Basile

reviews.text: For a company whose history is so steeped in gorgeously animated sincerity, “Pinocchio” emphasizes how Disney’s defining trait as of late is sheepishness.
reviews.author: David Lynch

reviews.text: It’s at least a thrill for the eyes and at best a lovely tribute updated in thoughtful and necessary ways. And, when all else fails, there’s always Tom Hanks.
reviews.author: Caitlin Wyneken

reviews.text: This latest adaptation feels heartless, rushed, and sloppily put together. It's a reboot that not even Tom Hanks can save.
reviews.author: Courtney Lanning

reviews.text: Impressive CGI and a vibrant colour palette aside, it’s hard to find a genuine reason for anyone to devote an evening to experience what little Pinocchio brings to the table.
reviews.author: Rhys Bowen Jones

reviews.text: ... A remake that is as unnecessary as it is opportunistic.
reviews.author: Elsa Fernández-Santos

reviews.text: A valiant attempt, but the small mistakes made are plenty and do add up.
reviews.author: Doug Walker

reviews.text: Jiminy appears to be wearing another cricket’s face as a mask.
reviews.author: Matt Pais

reviews.text: [Movies like Pinocchio are] some strange form of flattery, films that exist solely to remind of us the same, better film, that existed previously.
reviews.author: Tom Santilli

reviews.text: Pinocchio feels somewhat empty. Zemeckis is almost able to convey some magic through cinematography and certain solid visuals, but there is nothing added that allows it to feel fresh or even necessary.
reviews.author: Austin Burke

reviews.text: As with Aladdin, Dumbo, The Jungle Book, Pete's Dragon, The Lion King and Mulan, the makeover of Pinocchio served up here features top-class digital animation but simply lacks the spark, novelty, pace and magic of the original.
reviews.author: Jim Schembri

reviews.text: As a re-imagined classic, Pinocchio falls short of investing enough imagination into its version of the source material to make it feel special.
reviews.author: Rick Marshall

reviews.text: An efficient retread that doesn’t stray too far from the 1940 original.
reviews.author: Andy Lea

reviews.text: You just feel so little for this version of Pinocchio or the human father who pines for him to return.
reviews.author: Nick Allen

reviews.text: A well-intentioned work that largely falls flat, it arrives as just another widget in Disney’s “remake ’em all!” agenda, one whose pedigree offered the hope of something better.
reviews.author: John DeFore

reviews.text: In terms of its morals and messaging, this version does what it needs to do. But the magic is missing.
reviews.author: Allen Almachar

reviews.text: This Pinocchio has that Disney magic we crave, albeit a bit more hollowed than one would expect.
reviews.author: M.N. Miller

reviews.text: All in all, if you like the 1940, Disney version of Pinocchio… just watch that one.... Ultimately, Pinocchio is little more than superfluous fluff from a movie studio with a legendary past of telling much better stories.
reviews.author: Kimberly Pierce

reviews.text: More than anything, I’m confused. Confused as to what the filmmakers actually wanted to do with this material. There’s no new take, no new angle, no clear takeaway with this version. And so all we get is a wooden shell. Knock knock. Who’s there? Nobody.
reviews.author: Kevin L. Lee

reviews.text: No matter what your opinion is on the discussion surrounding these live-action adaptations, Zemeckis’ updating feels fresh and innovative.
reviews.author: Jeanne Kaplan

reviews.text: Today’s technology greatly enhances the experience of seeing PINOCCHIO again. The group’s eventual escape on Geppetto’s fishing boat through the monster’s mouth and the swirling ocean waters is exciting and remarkable.
reviews.author: David Kaplan

reviews.text: For those of us invested in the power of art, its commodification in films like Pinocchio is a huge bummer.
reviews.author: Steve Katz

reviews.text: Disney’s latest remake Pinocchio is the worst of these remakes and quite possibly one of the worst movies the studio has ever made
reviews.author: Rachel Wagner

reviews.text: This 2022 Pinocchio is a weird mix of over-adherence to what has come before and changes reaching for a modern sensibility, but it never makes an effort to do either entirely.
reviews.author: Julian Lytle

reviews.text: While it makes some vast improvements to problematic scenes and material in the original 1940 film, holy smoke-io, it adds almost as many unnecessary and frustratingly bonkers new changes.
reviews.author: Kirsten Acuna

reviews.text: The result is both Zemeckis &Hanks being limited by having to follow a clinically-made script, with no real emotion or feeling beyond what we're supposed to be feeling. Full review in Spanish.
reviews.author: Jorge Rivera Rubio

reviews.text: Watching how Pinocchio's nose grows in Disney's original 1940 Pinocchio movie is more interesting to look at than this unnecessary Pinocchio movie remake from filmmaker Robert Zemeckis ... Pinocchio should hold his nose for being in this stinker movie.
reviews.author: Carla Hay

reviews.text: This Pinocchio isn’t without charm, but it ultimately feels like calculated rehash with nothing new and inspired to add to the story.
reviews.author: John Serba

reviews.text: The verbal jokes for adults barely raise a smile, but Zemeckis visually remains the pro he’s always been, moving smoothly through a stylised world.
reviews.author: Jake Wilson

reviews.text: Aside from the cinematic upgrade and addition of a diverse cast, the film doesn't offer much in terms of novelty. Perhaps we should stop calling them "remakes" and refer to them as "upgrades" or the "pimped out version."
reviews.author: Lupe Rodriguez Haas

reviews.text: Think of this Pinocchio, at its best, as Zemeckis’s conglomerate-backed cultural critique, a nauseated state of the artistic union typified by a scene in which our little timber-carved innocent quizzically contemplates a steaming pile of horse dung.
reviews.author: Keith Uhlich

reviews.text: Mostly, Pinocchio itself washes ashore into a kind of no-man's land -- too uninspired to bring anything fresh to the material, dutifully playing like a pallid redo of the 1940 classic.
reviews.author: Brian Lowry

reviews.text: A complete waste of Hanks' evergreen charisma, and a storytelling approach that's fragmented and less than engaging.
reviews.author: Jim Judy

reviews.text: Neither imaginative enough to be refreshingly different nor faithful enough to be nostalgically satisfying, it falls into the...mediocre middle ground...winding up as a cinematic footnote one would rather skip over.
reviews.author: Frank Swietek

reviews.text: Tom Hanks and Robert Zemeckis team up again with a top animation team to bring the classic tale to new life in this endearing live action/CGI combo on Disney+.
reviews.author: Christopher Lloyd

reviews.text: The effect is an awkward fusion of fake and real that strains to find any magic in between. This Pinocchio, unfortunately, is no real boy, at all.
reviews.author: Jake Coyle

reviews.text: This remake of Pinocchio, like many of Disney’s live action remakes, offers no compelling reason for its existence. Anyone who wants to relive memories of watching the original as a child should just revisit it; it’s a classic for a reason.
reviews.author: Alex Bentley

reviews.text: The reimagining goes awry in the opening number — not “When You Wish Upon a Star,” the Oscar-winner that ascended to become the company’s signature tune, but a new ballad, “When He Was Here With Me,” sung by Geppetto about his freshly concocted dead son.
reviews.author: Amy Nicholson

reviews.text: An exercise in mimicry that could have been everything it wanted to, but has settled for an unbearable laziness. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Randy Meeks

reviews.text: A top-to-bottom embarrassment with no good reason to exist.
reviews.author: Josh Spiegel

reviews.text: A massive misfire. The animation is ugly and disturbing, with plastic looking characters and equally ghastly voice performances. Gordon-Levitt is terrible as Jiminy Cricket, giving a whiny, strained turn as one of the story’s most cherished characters.
reviews.author: Louisa Moore

reviews.text: ...for the most part, things shuffle along charmingly enough for a welcome but hardly necessary reimagining of Collodi’s text—at least until they really, really do not.
reviews.author: Luke Y. Thompson

reviews.text: The animation is now so hyper-advanced, the landscape of the movie so eerily both this and that, it is easy to get confused about where reality stops and ones and zeros take over.
reviews.author: Danny Leigh

reviews.text: Like Disney’s tepid 2019 live-action remake of “The Lion King,” it’s virtually a beat-by-beat remake of the original, but without the original’s energy and movement.
reviews.author: G. Allen Johnson

reviews.text: There’s a reason Disney chose to not allow critics to talk about this film until the day of release; the additional new songs and characters all slow down the pacing and the story doesn't effectively translate from animation to live-action visuals.
reviews.author: Jason Escamilla

reviews.text: Like the titular puppet at its center, Pinocchio lingers in an existential purgatory.
reviews.author: Christy Lemire

reviews.text: Sure, there are visual highlights and a few choices that make it watchable enough for Disney+ audiences, but how much good is there in a venture like this when the 1940 classic does everything better?
reviews.author: Aaron Neuwirth

reviews.text: With little personality and barely anything valuable to say about the world, the live-action Pinocchio remake is what Harry Styles would describe as something that ‘feels like a movie’.
reviews.author: Rohan Naahar

reviews.text: Pinocchio lacks charm and something fresh. I hope I’m wrong about this and that Pinocchio will entertain new audiences and families, but I'm afraid I'm not.
reviews.author: Tania Lamb

reviews.text: One just keeps wondering what the point of this redundant venture is, and ... it's hard to pinpoint one of substance or much worth.
reviews.author: Mark Dujsik

reviews.text: With few memorable sequences and inferior storytelling from its director, this adaptation falls flat. Families might find some joy in this, but hopefully, they’ll spend their time revisiting the classic film instead.
reviews.author: Alan French

reviews.text: While many of us have seen and heard this story countless times, Zemeckis offers a heart-filled, semi-fresh, and reasonably sanitized take that maintains the charm of the original.
reviews.author: Keith Garlington

reviews.text: A perfectly entertaining viewing experience, but nothing more.
reviews.author: Brian Orndorf

reviews.text: His new live-action Pinocchio adaptation gives you what you’d expect, but so, so much more. It’s as if Zemeckis wanted his adaptation to play like if Moulin Rouge-era Baz Luhrmann directed Willy Wonka and the Chocolate Factory.
reviews.author: Cory Woodroof

reviews.text: A solidly fanciful fable that vibrantly, creatively dusts off the years from pop culture’s most famous puppet.
reviews.author: Neil Pond

reviews.text: Pinocchio at times is every bit as charming and whimsical as you’d hope. At others, it suffers from leaning too much into spectacle, especially in the film’s second half, when “Pinocchio” can feel a bit hollow.
reviews.author: Mark Meszoros

reviews.text: This entire review may seem like faint praise, but the truth is that this incarnation of a boy who just wants to be real is as emotionally effective as the original, and rarely feels heretical...
reviews.author: Ryan Silberstein

reviews.text: Overall, [Robert] Zemeckis’ CGI/live-action version of Pinocchio is a missed opportunity with only a few worthwhile moments salvaging it from becoming a complete disaster.
reviews.author: Casey Chong

reviews.text: While a murky, laborious affair, Pinocchio never feels wholly inept with the consummate craftsman at the helm, yet it’s certainly the director’s laziest time behind the camera.
reviews.author: Jordan Raup

reviews.text: It doesn't take a Blue Fairy to look into his hollow eyes and realize that he has a long way to go before becoming a real boy.
reviews.author: Phil Villarreal

reviews.text: A joyless exercise in obligatory adaptation. If this is Hollywood's idea of a live-action Pinocchio, they all owe Roberto Benigni an apology.
reviews.author: Fred Topel

reviews.text: A wooden live-action remake.
reviews.author: Matt Singer

reviews.text: As bland and uninspired as you've probably come to expect from these tepid live-action re-imaginings.
reviews.author: Evan Dossey

reviews.text: Visual masterpiece with subtle nods towards mental health. Watch for the nostalgia, but don't expect this to be a Monstro whale of a movie. There's a reason this movie went straight to streaming
reviews.author: Christie Cronan

reviews.text: The filmmakers don't pad too much length to the film and aside from some songs and other changes, it feels like you're watching a remixed version of the animated film--just in live-action
reviews.author: Danielle Solzman

reviews.text: Visually stunning at times, there's a robotic undercurrent that somehow makes the film feel lifeless even as the titular puppet is brought to life.
reviews.author: Graeme Guttmann

reviews.text: If the 1940 Pinocchio showed that any wish your heart desires could come true, this remake shows what happens when your nightmares come to life.
reviews.author: Ross Bonaime

reviews.text: Pinocchio is a soulless monstrosity that trades dreams for nightmares.
reviews.author: Maggie Lovitt

reviews.text: Following in the footsteps of other Disney live-action remakes like Beauty and the Beast, The Lion King and The Jungle Book, the latest version of Pinocchio adds new technology to the story, but no new ideas.
reviews.author: Richard Crouse

reviews.text: It may not have surprised me, story-wise, but Pinocchio made me glad that I'm flesh and blood.
reviews.author: Peter Martin

reviews.text: Zemeckis ably adapts one of Disney’s classic tales in a way that acknowledges full well that everything that played for kids 82 years ago still works today.
reviews.author: Edward Douglas

reviews.text: Another soulless and unimaginative Disney remake.
reviews.author: Nate Adams

reviews.text: The journey of one affable puppet’s search for an identity has never felt so charmless and devoid of humanity onscreen.
reviews.author: Matt Conway

reviews.text: Follows the original Disney version fairly faithfully, albeit with some additional songs and more amped-up action.
reviews.author: Alistair Harkness

reviews.text: Zemeckis can be a superb director, yet he gives in to his worst technology-driven impulses here, effectively sucking all meaning out of the tale.
reviews.author: Mike McGranaghan

reviews.text: Though not without charm, and some splendid CGI, this scattershot grab-bag of good intentions results in a bit of an emotional flatline. This puppet will not tug on your heartstrings.
reviews.author: Alex Godfrey

reviews.text: Pinocchio further proves that Walt Disney Pictures’ obstinate effort to remake all of its classic animated films into hybrid, live-action/computer-animated versions is an exercise in mediocrity.
reviews.author: Tara Bennett

reviews.text: Every frame of “Pinocchio” is filled with rich and lush detail — at times this almost looks like a 3-D film — and the performances, whether live action or voiced, are universally excellent.
reviews.author: Richard Roeper

reviews.text: An entirely unnecessary “live-action” remake of the animated classic, Zemeckis’s film accomplishes a number of cinematic achievements, none of them commendable.
reviews.author: Barry Hertz

reviews.text: Another enjoyable yet flawed addition to Disney’s live-action catalog, with stunning visuals that capture the magic of the original but ultimately fail to keep up the pace.
reviews.author: Fay Watson

reviews.text: By skillfully manipulating the lines of reality, Zemeckis creates a film worthy of its visual efforts, one with a mostly real purpose: To update the film for contemporary audiences.
reviews.author: B.L. Panther

reviews.text: The Blue Fairy may have brought life to Pinocchio, but no one here is delivering anything particularly fresh.
reviews.author: John Anderson

reviews.text: Pinocchio’s nose isn’t all that’s wooden and too long here.
reviews.author: Mark Feeney

reviews.text: [A] garish, dead-eyed exercise, which recreates the 1940 masterpiece largely scene for scene, albeit with a handful of instantly forgettable minor detours.
reviews.author: Robbie Collin

reviews.text: Each failed attempt to modernize its beautiful message serves as a reminder of how little it needed updating in the first place.
reviews.author: Christian Zilko

reviews.text: You may not have asked for a live-action remake of Pinocchio, but now you’ve got one, and it’s still as weird, surreal, and morally pompous as the original.
reviews.author: Shannon Connellan

reviews.text: Some films feel like classics from the start. Others don’t. The new “Pinocchio” falls into the latter category. Watching it makes you believe sometimes it’s best to leave well enough alone.
reviews.author: Bill Goodykoontz

reviews.text: As with so many of the director’s previous CGI extravaganzas, all the meticulous surface detail in the world can’t compensate for the core emptiness of the film’s digital creations.
reviews.author: Andrew Barker

reviews.text: Zemeckis’ “Pinocchio” prompts one to wish upon a star that Disney would stop diluting the legacy of its beloved animated features with these soulless knockoffs.
reviews.author: Carlos Aguilar

reviews.text: Something is off – the film is competently crafted, dutifully acted, clearly labored over with soul, and yet, like its star, lacks a beating heart.
reviews.author: Adrian Horton

reviews.text: Pinocchio the film lacks the same thing as Pinocchio the puppet. A heart.
reviews.author: Joey Morona

reviews.text: When you wish upon a remake. Makes no difference how bland and fake.
reviews.author: Travis Hopson

reviews.text: The result is the worst of both worlds, a movie that captures none of the wonder and joy of the 1940 film while also failing to update or reassess it in any worthwhile way.
reviews.author: Josh Bell

reviews.text: There may be no strings to hold Pinocchio down, but there sure are strings on Robert Zemeckis, pumping out Disney live-action remake disposable junk
reviews.author: Robert Kojder

reviews.text: Even with the always-reliable Tom Hanks as Geppetto, this new version of Pinocchio ironically never comes to life.
reviews.author: Ian Sandwell

reviews.text: Grim, psychosexual fairy tales like “Pinocchio” can still be effective, of course, if the tellers respect the primal feelings and fears they evoke. But if they hedge with warmth or whimsy, the results curdle quickly.
reviews.author: Elizabeth Weitzman

reviews.text: Remake of the classic Disney animation sanitizes the aging cartoon's more dubious elements, but still manages to be bizarre as all get-out -- and in fact, this awkward mishmash of digital effects and live action adds new levels of weird.
reviews.author: Richard Trenholm

reviews.text: In a word, lesser. No part of this movie that replicates the original is in any way better, and the additions are lesser than anything in the original film.
reviews.author: Dan Murrell

reviews.text: Pretty much a shot for shot remake, this is an ok watch but hardcore fans will be frustrated by the unnecessary changes.
reviews.author: Tessa Smith

reviews.text: Absolutely charming, not to mention above and beyond for a direct-to-streaming movie.  Tom Hanks is always great but Joseph Gordon-Levitt & Keegan-Michael Key are the standouts here. Definitely has the Disney Magic!
reviews.author: Grace Randolph

reviews.text: Several scenes stand out including when Pinocchio and Geppetto are trapped inside the whale, and when Pinocchio is in Pleasure Island.
reviews.author: Allison Rose

reviews.text: We’re not sure how we got here, but yes, Disney just ruined Pinocchio. A movie it appears the studio didn’t bother finishing before dumping it on streaming, this remake will crush longtime fans and disappoint everyone else. Happy Disney+ Day.
reviews.author: Josh Wilding

reviews.text: Outside of the stellar Pleasure Island segment, this is a really dull feature that takes all the problems of the original film and makes them stand out even more.
reviews.author: Carson Timar

reviews.text: A sweet and charming retelling which breathes new life into this iconic tale and expands its narrative, often with bizarre choices. While it never manages to even touch the magic of the classic, it is a reasonably enjoyable Disney remake.
reviews.author: Dave Lee

synopsis: Academy Award® winner Robert Zemeckis directs this live action and CGI retelling of the beloved tale of a wooden puppet who embarks on a thrilling adventure to become a real boy. Tom Hanks stars as Geppetto, the woodcarver who builds and treats Pinocchio (Benjamin Evan Ainsworth) as if he were his real son. Joseph Gordon-Levitt is Jiminy Cricket, who serves as Pinocchio’s guide as well as his "conscience"; Academy Award® nominee Cynthia Erivo is the Blue Fairy; Keegan-Michael Key is "Honest" John; Academy Award® nominee Lorraine Bracco is Sofia the Seagull, a new character, and Luke Evans is The Coachman.
